payload.statement: No retrieved study tests BTK R288W in cells or in full-length protein for kinase activity, PLCγ2 phosphorylation, BLNK association or membrane recruitment; the binding evidence comes from an isolated SH2 domain and synthetic phosphopeptides.

payload.summary: The strongest mechanistic evidence for BTK p.Arg288Trp is E15 (PMID:11206059), which reports that R288 lies in the SH2 phosphotyrosine binding site and that R288 mutants lose more than 200-fold phosphopeptide binding. E16–E18 give PH-domain and structural context, and E19 reports R288W in a patient cohort without any functional assay. Gaps G1–G2 record that no retrieved study tests R288W folding, stability or cellular signalling, so loss of function via SH2 binding is supported only at the isolated-domain level.

BTK p.Arg288Trp (Q06187) collect is done: E1-E14 cover ClinVar and UniProt variant classes, the SH2 domain and helix annotations, AlphaMissense, ScoreCons, popEVE and EVE values, two experimental structures (6HTF, 2GE9), the AlphaFold model, and the ClinVar R288Q record at the same residue. G1-G3 record that no residue-level functional assay exists, that neither experimental structure carries the mutation or a ligand, and that the variant is not observed in gnomAD v4.1. Consistency check reports 18 evidence items in the store; E15-E18 were not recorded by me in this run, so their origin should be verified. Duplicates are by design (UniProtKB Q06187 for E3/E4 and EBI ProtVar Q06187:288:W for E8/E9, different facts); no items lack a source, and no hypotheses exist yet, so all items are unlinked.

Step 2 HYPOTHESES. Subject: variant_id=BTK-p.Arg288Trp gene=BTK accession=Q06187 position=288 reference=R alternate=W. payload.statement: The R288W substitution removes the positively charged guanidinium of Arg288, which lines the phosphotyrosine-binding pocket of the BTK SH2 domain. Without it, the SH2 domain cannot engage the phosphotyrosine motif of partner proteins, so the mutant fails to recruit BTK to its signalling partners.
payload.would_refute: A model of a phosphotyrosine peptide docked into the SH2 pocket (built from 6HTF or 2GE9 geometry, or from AF-Q06187-F1) places Arg288 more than about 4.5 Å from the phosphate group, or the W288 model keeps peptide docking energy and contacts equal to wild type. Refutation also follows if ligand-bound SH2 structures show no pY-pocket contact at residue 288.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: E15 is the only retrieved assay that tests R288 directly, and it links this pocket to a more than 200-fold loss of phosphopeptide binding. It is a combined R288/R307 mutant result on an isolated SH2 domain with synthetic peptides, so attribution to R288 alone is uncertain. E10 and E11 show no non-solvent ligand, so no pocket-bound ligand is observed; this does not refute the mechanism but leaves the pocket geometry unverified. Missing: a separate R288W binding measurement, a pY-peptide complex containing this residue, and full-length or cellular data (G5).

payload.statement: The Arg-to-Trp change in the SH2 helix (288-298) disrupts local packing and salt-bridge networks, so the SH2 domain misfolds or becomes less stable, which reduces expression or folding of the full-length kinase.
payload.would_refute: Predicted stability change for R288W (for example FoldX or ESM-based ΔΔG) is within about ±1 kcal/mol of wild type, the AF-Q06187-F1 helix 288-298 keeps its pLDDT and backbone geometry, and Arg288 is solvent-exposed with no buried partner in 6HTF or 2GE9. Refutation also follows if the variant's side chain makes no intra-domain contact in the experimental structures.
payload.label: agent-generated hypothesis
payload.rank_rationale: The predictors (E6, E8, E9) and conservation (E7) all point to damage, but they score pathogenicity without naming a mechanism. E4 places residue 288 in a helix that is experimentally supported, which gives a plausible route to destabilisation. No retrieved study measures folding or stability of R288W (G4), and the one binding study is on the wild-type SH2 domain. This leaves stability as a plausible second explanation with no direct test yet.

payload.summary: Two agent-generated hypotheses are recorded for BTK R288W. H1 (protein_interaction, rank 1): loss of the Arg288 phosphotyrosine-pocket contact in the SH2 domain, supported by E15 and tested by pY-peptide docking on 6HTF/2GE9 or AF-Q06187-F1. H2 (stability_folding, rank 2): destabilisation of the SH2 helix 288-298, supported by the predictors E6/E8/E9 and E4, tested by ΔΔG and helix geometry. Gaps G4 and G5 (no stability or cellular data for R288W) and G1 (no residue-level functional assay) remain open. Note that the literature handoff cited G1-G2 in error; its gaps are G4-G5.

payload.description: FoldX predicted folding free-energy change for R288W on the AlphaFold model (via ProtVar), with pLDDT at residue 288 and the same predictor for other substitutions at 288. Discriminates H2 (destabilisation of the SH2 helix) from H1 (loss of pY-pocket charge with a stable fold). A destabilising value supports H2; a neutral value weakens H2 and leaves H1 as favourite.
payload.expected_learning_reasoning: H2 is the only hypothesis this test can move. A destabilising result (at or above about 1 kcal/mol) would raise H2 and make H1 and H2 close, since both could contribute. A neutral result would lower H2 and confirm H1 as favourite. It cannot move H1 directly, and a neutral FoldX value is weak evidence against misfolding, so the outcome shifts the ranking by a moderate amount. Not 1.0 because H1 is not directly tested.

payload.summary: T1 (FoldX stability_effect on AF-Q06187-F1) recorded as E20 and E21, both computational_prediction and linked to T1, H1 and H2. R288W ΔΔG is +5.68 kcal/mol (predicted_destabilising, pLDDT 85.06); R288G +0.49 and R288Q +0.13 are the within-site comparison. Consistency: 21 evidence items, none uncited; E20/E21 reuse the ProtVar Q06187:288:W record already cited by E8/E9 (E21 also carries the G and Q values, which have their own ProtVar entries not cited). E14, E16, E17, E18 and E19 are not linked to any hypothesis. H1 and H2 still read latest_verdict "untested"; T1 is a single computational prediction, so the verdicts are for you to set.

per_hypothesis.why: T1 measures folding free energy, not phosphotyrosine binding, so it does not test the SH2 pocket model. The would_refute criterion (docked pY more than about 4.5 Å from Arg288, or equal W288 docking energy) was not evaluated. Context only: the same predictor gives R288Q a ΔΔG of +0.13 kcal/mol, so the destabilisation is driven by the Trp side chain, not by loss of charge. That does not bear on H1's binding mechanism either way.

FoldX ΔΔG for R288W is +5.68 kcal/mol on AF-Q06187-F1, above the 2.0 kcal/mol destabilising threshold (verdict predicted_destabilising). Applicability passed: residue pLDDT 85.06. Within-site comparison: R288G +0.49 and R288Q +0.13 kcal/mol, so this substitution stands out at the site. The would_refute criterion (|ΔΔG| within about 1 kcal/mol) was not met, so H2 is not refuted. Consistent with E4 (helix 288-298), E13 (pLDDT 84.44) and E6-E9 (computational pathogenicity signals).

payload.uncertainty: T1 is one computational FoldX estimate on one predicted model. FoldX errors on predicted models are near 1 kcal/mol, so +5.68 is well outside that band, but it is still not a measurement. The missense3d result (Neutral) conflicts with the FoldX call and is not explained by the record; treat it as a disagreement, not as support for either side. A neutral stability call does not show the variant is tolerated, and this test cannot show whether destabilisation reduces expression, causes misfolding in cells, or is only one part of the loss of function. ClinVar also lists R288Q as pathogenic (E14) while FoldX calls R288Q nearly neutral (+0.13), so a folding-only model does not explain the whole residue, and a binding mechanism (H1) may still contribute. The runner returned no job ID or manifest URL; provenance rests on results/T1.json and the reproducible command in the record, so the run cannot be independently traced to a remote job. Validation still needed: an independent stability predictor (for example ESM-based or a second FoldX run with repair), and a wet-lab expression or thermal-stability measurement of R288W.

payload.why: Previous favourite H1 (protein interaction): its direct support is residue-level, not substitution-level. E15 (PMID 11206059) reports that R288 and R307 in the phosphotyrosine pocket cut peptide binding more than 200-fold, and E10/E11 show the residue at the SH2 pocket. No measurement exists for R288W binding, and T3 (ligand contact) is not feasible (feasibility 0). Strongest rival H2 (stability/folding): T1 (predicted_destabilising, ΔΔG +5.68 kcal/mol, residue pLDDT 85.06, within-site R288G +0.49 and R288Q +0.13) gives a measured value for this exact substitution that passed its applicability control, and does not meet H2's refutation criterion. E4, E13 and E6-E9 already supported H2. Given that T1 adds the only direct R288W number and H1 has no direct R288W binding measurement, H2 now has the stronger direct support. This is a computational prediction, not an experiment, and E14 (R288Q pathogenic, FoldX near neutral) means H1 is not excluded. Evidence: T1, E4, E13, E15, E14.

Outcome that supports H2 (and weakens H1): distance under about 4.5 Å for the reference and no pocket contact or change in peptide docking energy for W288. Outcome that refutes H1: distance above about 4.5 Å or equal docking energy for W288 versus reference. Report the job ID or manifest URL if the runner returns one.

## Question
Which molecular mechanism best explains the loss of function of BTK p.Arg288Trp, and does one targeted computational test change the starting conclusion? [E1, E2]

## Evidence
ClinVar and UniProtKB both record R288W as pathogenic for X-linked agammaglobulinemia [E1, E2]. Residue 288 lies in the SH2 domain and in a helix at 288–298 [E3, E4, E10, E11]. AlphaMissense and EVE score the variant as pathogenic; these are computational predictions [E6, E9]. No retrieved study measures folding or expression of full-length R288W, or tests it in cells or for kinase activity [G4, G5]. Residue 288 has no functional assay on record, and the variant is absent from gnomAD v4.1 [G1, G3]. In an isolated SH2 domain, mutation of R288 cut phosphopeptide binding more than 200-fold [E15].

## Agent-generated hypotheses
- H1 (protein interaction, starting rank 1): loss of the pocket arginine stops the SH2 domain from engaging phosphotyrosine partners [H1].
- H2 (stability/folding, starting rank 2): the Arg-to-Trp change in the SH2 helix destabilises the domain and reduces folding or expression [H2].

## Tests considered and the choice
The planner chose T1, a FoldX stability test, over T2 (structural context), T3 (ligand contact, infeasible) and T4 (structure comparison, needs approval and has low learning) [plan seq 39].

## Result
Round 1, T1: FoldX predicts ΔΔG +5.68 kcal/mol for R288W on the AlphaFold model, above the 2.0 threshold, with residue pLDDT 85.06. Same-site controls were R288G +0.49 and R288Q +0.13 [T1, E20, E21]. This is a prediction, not a measurement. The favourite moved from H1 before the test to H2 after it, and the decision changed [decision seq 54]. The reopening was recorded [note seq 57].

Round 2, T2: residue 288 falls in ProtVar predicted pockets but in none of the P2Rank pockets, and in no predicted interface [T2, E22, E23, E24]. This weakens H1 without refuting it. H2 is unchanged [decision seq 75].

## Updated decision
Favoured: H2 (stability/folding), an agent-generated hypothesis supported so far only by computational predictions [H2, T1]. The favourite changed in round 1 and stayed the same in round 2 [decisions seq 54, seq 75].

## Uncertainty and validation still needed
FoldX errors on predicted models are near 1 kcal/mol [E20], so the +5.68 value is a prediction that has not been validated experimentally [T1]. missense3d calls R288W neutral, which conflicts with FoldX [E21]. ClinVar lists R288Q as pathogenic [E14], but FoldX calls R288Q near-neutral [E21], so folding alone may not explain the whole residue. The runner returned no job ID or manifest, so the run cannot be traced to a remote job [T1, T2]. Both hypotheses still need experimental testing.

## Next experiment
Computational: test whether a phosphotyrosine peptide docks near Arg288 in the reference and W288 models [next_experiments seq 55]. Laboratory: compare melting temperature and soluble yield of wild-type and R288W SH2 constructs, with a binding readout for H1 [next_experiments seq 76].
